newsitem.title: FRANCE: French business sees improvement - BoF survey.
newsitem.headline: French business sees improvement - BoF survey.

text.p: French industry leaders said they saw significant improvement in all sectors in the months ahead, according to a Bank of France survey in January.

"The outlook for the coming months is distinctly brighter. Activity should increase in all sectors, with marked improvement in the intermediate goods and food-processing sectors," the Bank said in a statement.

The Bank said investment plans for 1997 appear to be less ambitious on the whole compared with capital spending plans at the same period in 1996. Nevertheless, the business leaders polled in January were more confident about future activity than they were a few months earlier, the Bank said.

"This could mean that previously postponed investment plans may be implemented in the coming months. However, plans for increasing output capacity remained few and far between, owing to the spare capacity currently available, and depend on stronger growth in demand," the Bank's statement said.

"In January, according to the business leaders surveyed by the Banque de France, industrial output continued to grow in most sectors. Activity was especially buoyant in the intermediate goods and consumers goods sectors. The food-processing sector was alone in recording a contraction in activity."
The Bank said overall demand strengthened more in January and that French products were very competitive on foreign markets.
Order books were considered near normal levels overall, but still low in the food-processing and car industries. They were considered satisfactory in the capital goods and consumer goods sectors.

"Inventories of finished products are gradually returning to normal overall, but they still exceed the desired levels in the consumer goods, food-processing and intermediate goods sectors," the Bank said.
The Bank said it surveys about 12,000 businesses each month to compile its survey. It said the comments in its survey apply to seasonally-adjusted data.
